concerns.text: The validation target `logP` is a calculated molecular descriptor derived directly from the SMILES/graph representation, yet the Random Forest baseline (FR‑005) is trained on the full set of standard descriptors **including `logP` itself**. This makes the target a predictor, creating a circular/tautological validation: the model can trivially learn the identity function, inflating performance and rendering the paired t‑test comparison with the GNN meaningless. The same issue applies to the GNN, which predicts a descriptor that is mathematically a function of its own input graph, so the hypothesis that “graph topology captures predictive information beyond standard descriptors” cannot be empirically tested with this design.
